newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices squeezed by further warnings.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices squeezed by further warnings.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended lower on Tuesday, squeezed by repeated warnings from the securities authorities about the risk of stock market volatility, brokers said.

In another apparent effort by Beijing to rein in the markets, the China Securities newspaper carried an article detailing the risks of investment in stocks, following on from similar warnings in all major securities newspapers on Monday.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.605 points or 0.82 percent to 73.320 on volume of 13.0 million shares worth $6.9 million.
The Shanghai A index slumped 31.027 points or 2.32 percent to 1,307.031 points on turnover of 9.7 billion yuan ($1.1 billion).
Falls on the A share market triggered some domestic profit-taking on the B share market, resulting in the B index dip, brokers said.
"Trading volume was thin today, indicating that downward potential is limited in the short term," said one broker.
Shanghai Rubber Belt was the biggest B share loser on selling by speculators, closing down $0.014 or 5.98 percent to $0.220 on volume of 2,600 shares.

Property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the most-traded on domestic profit-taking after continued gains over the past few days. It fell $0.018 or 1.71 percent to $1.032 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index lost 1.08 points or 0.67 percent to 159.33 on turnover of HK$64.57 million ($8.3 million).

"The B shares were pushed down by falls among their A share counterparts but the downward potential on the B share market is limited as it has only registered marginal rises since the beginning of this year," an analyst said.
"Whether the A share market continues to fall sharply depends on whether the securities authorities announce any specific measures," he added.
Among the Shenzhen B shares, Chiwan Wharf was the worst performer, falling HK$0.37 or 6.49 percent to close at HK$5.33 on volume of 138,700 shares.
According to its annual report released on Tuesday, the company posted a 14 percent drop in 1996 net profit and proposed a cash dividend of 0.169 yuan per share based on 1996 profits.
"Investors were disappointed by the company's dividend plan," a second analyst said.
On the Shanghai A share market, Kunming Machine Tool was the biggest loser on expectations of poor results, slumping 0.43 yuan or 7.47 percent to 5.32 yuan on volume of 5.9 million shares.
The Shenzhen A index fell 12.61 points or 2.69 percent to 456.38 on turnover of 11.7 billion yuan from Monday's 13.3 billion yuan.
